elicitation_input.question: What was the original profession of the novelist Joseph Conrad?

llm_generation.text:
Joseph Conrad, born Józef Teodor Konrad Korzeniowski, was originally a sailor—specifically, he worked in the merchant marine before becoming a novelist.

He spent about 20 years at sea, first with the French merchant marine and later with the British merchant navy, eventually earning his master mariner's certificate. He rose to the rank of captain and commanded his own ship, the Otago, during this maritime career. His extensive experience at sea, including voyages to places like the Congo, Southeast Asia, and other far-flung locations, deeply influenced his later literary work. Novels such as "Heart of Darkness," "Lord Jim," and "The Nigger of the 'Narcissus'" draw heavily on his nautical experiences and the places he visited during his years as a sailor.

Conrad only turned to writing fiction seriously in his late 30s, after retiring from the sea, and English—remarkably—was actually his third language, after Polish and French. Despite this, he became one of the most celebrated prose stylists in English literature.
